headline: Approved prior meeting minutes 6-0; discussed Commissioner Tobin's resignation, the chair's planned retirement, and vacancies.
summary: Commissioner Gerry Tobin resigned, effective immediately. Chairman David Schaefer plans to retire after the December meeting, and Commissioner Kathy Larson's term ends in December 2026. Members discussed filling vacancies, and a resident who applied to serve said he had not heard back.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the October 6, 2026 meeting, 6-0.
Agreed to send a letter thanking Commissioner Gerry Tobin for her service.

plain_text:
TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Farmington Canal Commission 
Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
7:00 PM, November 10, 2026 
 
 
 
Hamden Government 
Center 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel:  (203) 287-7070 
Fax:  (203) 287-7075 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL TO ORDER 
  
 The meeting was called to order by Chair Commissioner D. Schaefer at 7:12 PM. 
2. ATTENDANCE 
  
 The Clerk called the roll, and the following members were present: 
 
Present: 
 
Commissioner David Schaefer, Chairman 
Commissioner Nick Hansen 
Commissioner Peter Cyr 
Commissioner Kathy Larson 
Commissioner Jeffrey Campbell 
Commissioner David Radcliffe 
 
Resigned 
Commissioner Gerry Tobin 
 
Also in attendance were Briana J. Belton-Robinson, Boards and Commissions Clerk, and 2 
members of the public, Norm B. and Mike Melanson, who attended virtually. 
3. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES 
  
 Chairman D. Schaefer moved to adopt the minutes from Tuesday, October 6th, 2026. 
 
Commissioner made the motion to amend the previous agenda, and Commissioner 
seconded it. 
 
Vote by Roll Call: 
 
Yes 
Commissioner David Schaefer, Chairman 
Commissioner Nick Hansen
Commissioner Peter Cyr 
Commissioner Kathy Larson 
Commissioner Jeffrey Campbell 
Commissioner David Radcliffe 
 
No 
 
Absent 
 
Resigned 
Commissioner Gerry Tobin 
 
The motion passed. 
 
• Roll Call Vote Summary: Yes 6, No 0, Abstentions 0, Absent 0 
 
4. PUBLIC COMMENT 
  
 No public comments were taken during the designated public comment portion. Later in the 
meeting, Resident Michael Melanson spoke regarding his application to serve on the 
Commission; see New Business. 
5. CORRESPONDENCE 
There will be a brief summary of the correspondence submitted between the last 
correspondence update and this one. This includes but is not limited to any 
correspondence with council members that members wish to submit for the record. It can 
also include written communication to the council from the administration, community 
members, etc.   
 Chairman D. Schaefer reported receipt of Commissioner Geraldine Tobin’s resignation 
letter. He acknowledged her many years of service to the Commission, first as its clerk and 
later as a commissioner. The Boards & Commissions Clerk indicated that the resignation 
appeared to be effective immediately. 
 
Commissioner K. Larson stated that she had notified the Town of her intention to leave 
when her term expires in December 2026 and that the Town acknowledged her notice. She 
indicated that she would be unable to attend the December meeting. 
 
Commissioner P. Cyr asked whether the Town had received written follow-up proposals 
from the two residents who presented projects at the October meeting: the canal lending 
libraries and the interpretive memorial associated with a mural honoring Sylvie Sydney 
Rosenthal. The Boards & Commissions Clerk checked the Commission email account and 
reported that no requested follow-up submissions had been received. Commissioner P. Cyr 
indicated that he might contact the presenters. 
6. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 No executive session was held.
7. REPORTS 
  
 
 
  1. Report of the Chairman  
  Chairman D. Schaefer announced his intention to retire from the Commission, 
preferably after the December 2026 meeting, provided his departure would not 
prevent the Commission from meeting due to insufficient membership. He suggested 
placing the election of a new chairperson on the January 2027 meeting agenda. He 
stated that he would again contact the Mayor to request appointments to fill 
vacancies. 
 
Chairman D. Schaefer announced that he would receive an award from the Hamden 
Chamber of Commerce later that week recognizing his work with the Farmington 
Canal Commission. He reflected on the Commission’s earlier work involving 
engineering, easements, design approvals, construction, funding, and coordination 
with other agencies. He said he was organizing about 40 years of Commission files to 
transfer to his successor. 
 
In light of the Commission’s reduced workload, Chairman D. Schaefer suggested that 
future commissioners consider meeting every other month, with special meetings as 
necessary, subject to applicable meeting requirements. No one moved to change the 
meeting schedule. 
 
Chairman D. Schaefer reported revised Town procedures for agenda submissions 
and related correspondence, including submitting agendas three business days 
before the required posting deadline and copying the Town Clerk and Clerk’s Office. 
The Boards & Commissions Clerk confirmed that a meeting for board and commission 
chairpersons was scheduled for Thursday, November 12, from 5:30 to 6:30 pm, and 
agreed to forward the information to commissioners. She also agreed to inquire 
whether the session would be recorded. 
 
Chairman D. Schaefer proposed sending a letter thanking Commissioner G. Tobin for 
her service. Commissioners expressed support, and he agreed to prepare the letter. 
He also indicated that he intended to recognize Commissioner K. Larson’s service 
separately. 
 
 
 
8. OLD BUSINESS 
  
 The Commission revisited the two community proposals presented at its October meeting. 
No written proposals had yet been received, and no action was taken. 
9. NEW BUSINESS 
  
 Commissioner J. Campbell requested clarification on the process for filling Commission 
vacancies. Chairman D.Schaefer explained that commissioners are appointed by the 
Mayor and described prior practices of soliciting applications and seeking the Chair’s input.
Commissioner K. Larson noted that the application process is available on the Town of 
Hamden website and that she had shared the information publicly. 
 
Resident Michael Melanson stated that he submitted an application to the Mayor’s Office 
earlier in the year and was informed in September that appointments might move forward, 
but he had not received a subsequent update. Commissioner J. Campbell acknowledged 
his prior interest in serving. 
 
Chairman D. Schaefer emphasized the need for additional appointments to ensure the 
Commission could continue functioning. No appointment or other formal action occurred. 
10. ADJOURNMENT 
  
 Commissioner N. Hansen moved to adjourn. A seconded by Commissioner P. Cyr.   
 
The motion to adjourn passed unanimously. 
 
With no further business, the meeting adjourned at 7:30 pm.
